title: Kidnapping of businessman Jerry Boshoga
description: Kidnapping under investigation that led SAPS to search Matlala's Centurion residence on 6 December 2024; Matlala denied involvement during the subsequent interview.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Murder of DJ Sumbody
description: Sandton case (CAS 398/11/2022) later ballistically linked to the Bramley AK-47 seized in the Armand Swart investigation.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Murder of Don Tindleni
description: Orlando case ballistically linked to the same Bramley AK-47.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Murder of DJ Vintos
description: Orlando/Pretoria West case ballistically linked to both the Bramley AK-47 and the Taurus pistol.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Attempted murder of Tebogo Thobejane
description: Sandton case ballistically linked to the Bramley firearms and connected to the Matlala prosecution.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Benoni 'Smoke King Supermarket' kidnapping/extortion case
description: EMPD officers arrested by IPID inside Spies's own boardroom; provisionally withdrawn by the prosecutor in April 2025 after the complainant could not be traced.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Political Killings Task Team established
description: Ad hoc inter-disciplinary SAPS task team established administratively by the National Commissioner following an Inter-Ministerial Committee direction, to investigate political killings in KwaZulu-Natal. A predecessor provincial task team had been disbanded in May 2018 in consultation with the heads of SAPS, the NPA, the SSA and Correctional Services.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Moerane Commission of Inquiry reports
description: The KwaZulu-Natal provincial inquiry into political killings reported. Masemola and Khumalo both testified the PKTT was already in existence by this date and was not established as a result of this report.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Minister Cele's letter to the National Director of Public Prosecutions
description: Letter from then-Minister of Police Bheki Cele to NDPP Adv Batohi setting out challenges in KwaZulu-Natal political-killing cases, including witness-protection failures, questionable withdrawal decisions, delayed decisions and repeated bail grants, with recommendations for a dedicated court and dedicated prosecutors.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Directive 3 of 2019 issued by the DPP KwaZulu-Natal
description: Directive replacing Directive 1 of 2018, addressing coordination with the task team, dedicated prosecutorial capacity, use of section 204 witnesses and controls on withdrawals.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Katlehong-area murder / alleged scene clean-up
description: Murder at which Spies testified Mkhwanazi arrived and allegedly directed clean-up and body disposal; no officer has been charged and a participant has become a Section 204 state witness.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: News24 media query on EMPD blue lights
description: Journalist Jeff Wicks's query about municipally-registered, blue-lit vehicles linked to Matlala triggered EMPD's internal investigation into Julius Mkhwanazi.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Murder of Armand Swart at Q-Tech, Vereeniging
description: Engineer shot and killed at the Q-Tech office park in Duncanville, Vereeniging. Three men were arrested at Bramley about three hours later and a fourth at the Klip River R59 Engen garage. The investigation escalated into the Gauteng Counter Intelligence Operation.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Murder of Armand Swart
description: Engineer shot at his employer's Vereeniging premises; the case at the centre of Witness B's and the ballistics witnesses' evidence, allegedly linked to a Transnet/SK Group tender-fraud motive.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Bramley arrests (Tau, Kekana, Mabusela)
description: Same-day arrest at Bramley of three suspects found with an AK-47, a Taurus pistol, a CZ pistol and other firearms later ballistically linked to over two dozen other serious crimes.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: First court appearance of the Swart accused, Vereeniging Magistrate's Court
description: Witness A testified to a large show of support for Warrant Officer Tau at the appearance, and that he and a colleague were followed and intimidated by fellow police officers afterwards.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Meeting between Witness A and Maj-Gen Shibiri
description: Witness A testified that Shibiri referenced 'three envelopes flying around' available to secure bail for Tau — one for the two investigating officers, one for the Prosecutor and one for the Magistrate — and named a lawyer and an individual said to be linked to a cartel.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Senzo Mchunu takes office as Minister of Police
description: Appointment date referenced in evidence; Commissioner Khumalo raised but left unresolved the difference between the 3 July 2024 cabinet announcement and the actual assumption of office.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Prosecutor Coetzee's letter raising threats to Swart investigators
description: The Senior Public Prosecutor at Vereeniging Regional Court formally raised threats to the investigators on the Swart murder case and syndicate links, prompting the secondment of ten PKTT members to the Gauteng Counter Intelligence Operation.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Warrant Officer Tau granted bail
description: Bail of R10,000 granted at Vereeniging on medical grounds after an initial refusal. Witness A testified that Vusi Ndlala had forewarned him of the outcome the previous day and confirmed it before his own office knew.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Threat and Risk Assessment classifies the Swart investigating team as high risk
description: Assessment conducted by a Crime Intelligence colonel. An earlier assessment requested in mid-May 2024 was never followed up with results. Overnight police protection began on 5 September 2024.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Attempted handover of the Swart docket to the Cold Case Unit
description: Two officers, including Warrant Officer Deon Mulaudzi, verbally sought the docket without a letter; the investigators refused.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: MP Fadiel Adams lodges near-identical complaints in two provinces
description: Three cases opened in Cape Town on 29 October 2024 concerning Crime Intelligence vetting, the secret fund account and the Mokwele appointment, with the same allegations re-registered in Orlando, Johannesburg two days later.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Chief of Staff Nkabinde refers case dockets to IDAC under section 27 of the NPA Act
description: Letter listing six case numbers, sent before the ten-working-day extension requested by the SAPS Inspectorate had lapsed. The letter was not itself a compliant section 27 affidavit.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: SAPS Inspectorate concludes the interception allegations are unfounded
description: Follow-up information note signed on Lt-Gen Jacobs's behalf, also recording that the complainant had evaded requests for an affidavit.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Arrest of Katiso Molefe and search of Matlala's property
description: Joint operation assisted by seconded PKTT members. Molefe was arrested and charged with murder and conspiracy to commit murder; his bail was refused on 2 April 2025. Phone downloads obtained on his arrest were later used in evidence.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: 6 December 2024 combined takedown
description: Coordinated same-day arrest of Katiso Molefe at his Sandton/Sandhurst home and a search of Vusimuzi Matlala's Centurion residence (linked to the Boshoga kidnapping); the scene of alleged Hawks interference and multiple leak/tip-off allegations.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Brigadier Nkhwashu's visit to Katiso Molefe at Groenpunt prison
description: Nkhwashu allegedly visited detained Molefe claiming to be his brother-in-law, arriving in a vehicle with concealed number plates; captured on prison CCTV.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Matlala's urgent High Court application over seized items
description: Application alleging theft of a Rolex, MacBook and other items during the 6 December 2024 search; dismissed for lack of urgency 24 December 2024 and then withdrawn.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Firearms Control Act compliance inspection at Matlala's premises
description: Two-day Gauteng Counter Intelligence Operations inspection with armed escort following a high threat and risk assessment; firearms were confiscated for ballistic analysis and later returned. Matlala's urgent application for their return was withdrawn on the day of hearing, 24 December 2024.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: CAT VIP compliance inspection
description: 18-19 December 2024 inspection uncovering further firearm-permit and safe-access irregularities at CAT VIP; firearms seized for ballistic testing and later returned.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Minister Mchunu's letter directing disbandment of the PKTT
description: Letter to the National Commissioner directing that the PKTT be disestablished immediately on the stated basis that it was 'no longer required nor is it adding any value to policing', and also directing an immediate halt on filling vacant Crime Intelligence posts, for which no explanation was given. Mkhwanazi received it by WhatsApp on 2 January 2025; it was reported in the media before Masemola had seen it.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Ministerial letter disbanding the PKTT
description: Letter from the Minister of Police to the National Commissioner freezing Crime Intelligence posts and disbanding the PKTT; Khumalo testified he was not consulted and only received it officially 14 January 2025.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Political Killings Task Team disbanded
description: Then-Minister of Police Senzo Mchunu directed the disbandment of the Political Killings Task Team. Mchunu maintains the team was always time-bound; National Commissioner Masemola told the commission he learned of it by WhatsApp while on approved leave.

sources.publisher: Mail & Guardian
News24 / City Press

title: False 'kidnapping' complaint and TRT deployment at Silverton lab
description: A January night visit by Witness B and Captain Makgotloe to retrieve the ballistics report triggered a disputed kidnapping complaint and the deployment of a Tactical Response Team.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Masemola and Khumalo brief the Minister on the 'Big Five' syndicate
description: Briefing at which Lt-Gen Sibiya was named among senior SAPS officers said to be involved with a criminal syndicate. Masemola later directed the Commission to treat those allegations as unsubstantiated and under investigation.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Khumalo's cartel-links briefing to Minister Mchunu
description: Khumalo briefed the Minister on SAPS officers allegedly linked to a criminal cartel (naming Sibiya, Shibiri, Nkhwashu, Makgotle, and a fourth withheld name).

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Lt Gen Sibiya issues a disbandment letter under his own name
description: After bringing the letter to Masemola on two successive days and being refused, Sibiya issued the same letter himself without changing the due date of 16 January 2025. Masemola testified he became aware of it only in February or March 2025 and characterised it as defiance of his instruction to wind the team down gradually.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Sibiya's directive implementing PKTT disbandment
description: Letter from Lt-Gen Sibiya directing implementation of the disbandment, citing 'an assessment' Khumalo testified he was never shown.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Masemola submits his report to the Minister on the disbandment directive
description: Report dated for the due date of 20 January 2025 and delivered on the Minister's return, setting out the PKTT's successes and responding to the 31 December 2024 letter.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Masemola briefs President Ramaphosa on the disbandment instruction
description: Masemola testified the President was 'quite taken aback' to learn the team was being disbanded with no reasons given, and said he would speak to the Minister — contradicting the Minister's separate assertion that the President agreed with the disbandment.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Lt Gen Sibiya's letter to Lt Gen Senthumule on deactivation and docket transfer
description: Letter directing deactivation and disbandment of the national task team and determining what should happen to its dockets. The letter states that Sibiya was acting on the instruction of the Minister of Police.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Murder of a councillor in the iLembe district
description: Mkhwanazi testified that the Minister contacted District Commissioner Maj Gen Gopaul directly about the case being assigned to the PKTT, bypassing the National and Provincial Commissioners.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Mkhwanazi, Masemola and the Minister appear before the Portfolio Committee on Police
description: Appearance at which Mkhwanazi alleged the Minister knew Brown Mogotsi and the Minister denied it. Masemola testified the Minister repeated the denial to him and two Deputy Ministers afterwards.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Cape Town meeting on the PKTT wind-down plan
description: Meeting at which Lt-Gen Khumalo presented the PKTT's successes in an effort to dissuade the Minister. Masemola initially described an 'agreement' on where dockets should go and later corrected this to the Minister's preferred course. The plan was never finalised or signed.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Cape Town meeting on PKTT disbandment implementation
description: Meeting at which Khumalo's proposed gradual wind-down plan was opposed by the Minister's Chief of Staff and Sibiya, but supported by the National and a Deputy National Commissioner.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: 118 PKTT dockets handed to Lt Gen Senthumule
description: Handover on the instruction of Lt Gen Sibiya. A further three dockets were handed to SAPS head office on 10 April 2025, bringing the total to 121 on the task team's count and 123 on the head-office audit. On Day 7 the Evidence Leader put the dates as 28 March and 22 April, which Adv Harrison accepted.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Follow-up meeting on the disbandment plan
description: Meeting that ended abruptly, at which the Minister said the decision was political and that further engagement would be with Masemola only.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Katiso Molefe's bail proceedings
description: Bail denied 2 April 2025; granted on appeal by Acting Judge President Ledwaba in June 2025, with conditions Witness B considered too lenient.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Cancellation of the Medicare 24 SAPS health-risk-management contract
description: Contract cancelled following an audit revealing fronting and fraud. Letters concerning the termination appear in the Day 9 and Day 12 chat exhibits.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Arrest of Vusimuzi 'Cat' Matlala
description: Arrested on three counts of attempted murder and conspiracy to commit murder. Two cellular devices were seized with consent for extraction; the WhatsApp material recovered from them became the principal documentary evidence on Days 8, 9 and 12.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Mkhwanazi's letter to the DPP on unexecuted J50 warrants
description: Letter apologising for the failure to execute arrest warrants after the dockets were found to have been delivered to Pretoria. Adv Harrison testified it addressed only the docket removal and not the reported disestablishment of the task team.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Mkhwanazi's public media briefing
description: Briefing at which Mkhwanazi made public allegations of political interference and criminal infiltration of SAPS and the criminal justice system, prompting establishment of the Commission.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Minister Mchunu placed on special leave
description: Date recorded in Van Rooyen's statement; Firoz Cachalia was appointed Acting Minister of Police.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Masemola disapproves the funding request for a new investigating team
description: Request recommended through Maj-Gen Motsepe and Lt Gen Sibiya was disapproved. Masemola found the 121 dockets had not been investigated for some four months, and his handwritten note recorded that the dockets were supposed to be returned to their stations of origin.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Return of the PKTT dockets to KwaZulu-Natal
description: Masemola wrote to Mkhwanazi advising that the dockets would be returned. An audit found the great majority had no investigative work done on them while at head office, save minor status confirmations and one contact with victims in an Eastern Cape case.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Joint media statement by Minister Cachalia and National Commissioner Masemola
description: Statement agreeing the respective roles of Executive and Operational Authority and committing to submitting the PKTT dockets to the Commission and returning them to KwaZulu-Natal.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Unexplained night-time police visit to Witness B's home
description: Prompted 24-hour protection for Witness B and her family; reason not established on the record.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Commission does not sit; Day 10 adjourned
description: The Chairperson announced that General Khumalo had left the precinct at three minutes after nine that morning because he was unwell, and that the Commission had decided not to sit. No evidence was led.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Search-and-seizure raid on Lt-Gen Sibiya's home
description: Televised raid on Sibiya's home; CCTV/LPR evidence tendered Day 25 places his bakkie (registered to Scharnick/Skarnik Stuart James) leaving in convoy with an SAPS office BMW.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: In-camera application argued and ruled on
description: Application by the Evidence Leaders for certain evidence to be heard in camera, opposed by News24 and Daily Maverick through Willem De Klerk Attorneys. The Chairperson set a 9 p.m. filing deadline for written argument on Day 11; on Day 13 the media parties withdrew their opposition and the Commission ruled, on its own assessment, that the Day 13 and Day 14 hearings would be in camera.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Ruling on the format for hearing in-camera witnesses
description: Ruling issued by agreement between the Evidence Leaders and Daily Maverick/News24 governing the format for five in-camera witnesses over two weeks, including remote and off-camera testimony, use of an intermediary, and public release of transcripts after testimony. Amended on Day 15 to permit Witnesses A, B and C to testify publicly with voices unaltered, images not broadcast and names withheld.

sources.publisher: Judicial Commission of Inquiry — official transcript

title: Lt-Gen Mkhwanazi's public briefing on alleged political interference
description: The KwaZulu-Natal provincial commissioner publicly alleged that the Political Killings Task Team was closed to shield politicians and crime-linked suspects, that 121 dockets were removed, and that the team had uncovered links between syndicates, politicians, police and prosecutors. Minister Mchunu rejected the allegations as made 'without evidence' and called for an urgent, transparent investigation.

sources.publisher: Mail & Guardian

title: President announces the commission and places Minister Mchunu on leave
description: President Ramaphosa announced a commission of inquiry chaired by Justice Madlanga, assisted by Adv Sesi Baloyi SC and Adv Sandile Khumalo SC, and stated: 'I have decided to put the Minister of Police Mr Senzo Mchunu on a leave of absence with immediate effect.' Professor Firoz Cachalia was named to take up the acting police ministry.

sources.publisher: The Presidency (South Africa)

title: Commission established by Proclamation PR 269
description: The commission was formally established by Proclamation PR 269 published in Government Gazette 53048, with terms of reference covering infiltration of criminal syndicates into law enforcement, intelligence, prosecution authorities, the judiciary and correctional services. The National Assembly established its parallel ad hoc committee on the same date.

sources.publisher: Department of Justice and Constitutional Development
Parliament of South Africa

title: Commission hearings open with Mkhwanazi as first witness
description: The commission began taking evidence, with KwaZulu-Natal Provincial Commissioner Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi as its first witness, detailing the origins of the Political Killings Task Team.

sources.publisher: Eyewitness News
Eyewitness News

title: Crime Intelligence head describes an alleged 'Big Five' syndicate
description: Lt-Gen Dumisani Khumalo told the commission about an alleged Gauteng-based cartel operating through syndicates of ten to twelve members, naming Vusimuzi Matlala and Katiso Molefe. The allegations were made in testimony and have not been tested in court.

sources.publisher: eNCA

title: Change of chief evidence leader
description: Advocate Terry Motau SC stepped down as chief evidence leader and Advocate Matthew Chaskalson SC was appointed in his place. The commission said Motau departed on good terms and thanked him for his service.

sources.publisher: SAnews (SA Government News Agency)

title: Media and SANEF oppose blanket in-camera hearings
description: SANEF opposed a blanket in-camera application by the commission's evidence leaders, arguing that witness-protection needs should be assessed case by case; News24 and Daily Maverick opposed the proposed closed-proceedings order.

sources.publisher: SANEF
eNCA

title: Evidence on the movement of the 121 PKTT dockets
description: Mary Motsepe, SAPS head of serious and violent crimes, told the commission she was instructed to collect the 121 dockets from Crime Intelligence for an audit that could have been done in KwaZulu-Natal, and that missing witness statements were found. Sibiya says the dockets had been dormant and that reallocation followed an approved structure.

sources.publisher: Mail & Guardian

title: Senzo Mchunu gives evidence
description: The suspended Minister of Police rejected the allegations against him, saying 'I have never been accused of corruption, not once', and defended the disbandment of the task team as a time-bound administrative decision.

sources.publisher: IOL

title: Commission witness Marius van der Merwe killed
description: Van der Merwe was shot multiple times outside his Brakpan home in front of his family. President Ramaphosa condemned the killing on 6 December 2025, saying the circumstances suggested his testimony 'angered elements in our society who want to undermine the rule of law'.

sources.publisher: The Presidency (South Africa)

title: First interim report submitted and acted on
description: The commission submitted its first interim report on 17 December 2025, identifying prima facie evidence of wrongdoing among law-enforcement and municipal officials. On 29 January 2026 the President announced referrals of five SAPS officials and nine current and former Ekurhuleni employees, and directed that a special SAPS investigations task team be constituted.

sources.publisher: The Presidency (South Africa)
News24

title: Shadrack Sibiya cross-examined over several days
description: The suspended deputy national commissioner gave evidence and faced days of cross-examination, denying the allegations while acknowledging that he knew Vusimuzi Matlala and had shared confidential SAPS audit material with associates. He says he is being politically targeted.

sources.publisher: Mail & Guardian
Daily Maverick

title: Twelve senior SAPS officers arrested in the Medicare24 matter
description: Brigadier Rachel Matjeng was arrested alongside eleven other senior officers in the criminal matter concerning the R360-million Medicare24 SAPS health-services contract. These are proceedings in the ordinary courts, separate from the commission.

sources.publisher: IOL
Daily Maverick

title: National Commissioner Masemola placed on precautionary suspension
description: President Ramaphosa placed Gen Fannie Masemola on precautionary suspension pending the conclusion of his criminal case, appointing Lt-Gen Puleng Dimpane as acting national commissioner. Masemola faces four counts under the Public Finance Management Act in the Pretoria Magistrate's Court.

sources.publisher: TimesLIVE

title: Witness G testifies in camera on day 100
description: A protected witness known as Witness G gave evidence behind closed doors on safety grounds, after applying in March 2026 for identity protection and voice distortion.

sources.publisher: IOL
Eyewitness News

title: Brown Mogotsi arrested hours after appearing at the commission
description: A SAPS multidisciplinary team arrested Mogotsi on the evening of 15 May 2026, the day he appeared before the commission, on charges including defeating the ends of justice and unlawful possession of a firearm and ammunition.

sources.publisher: News24

title: Second interim report delivered and its referrals noted
description: The commission's second interim report recommended disciplinary proceedings and immediate investigation of alleged criminal conduct in relation to Lt-Gen Shadrack Sibiya, Witness G, Sgt Fannie Nkosi and Mr Brown Mogotsi, and an Inspector-General of Intelligence investigation into alleged off-the-books Crime Intelligence operations. The Presidency noted the recommendations on 6 August 2026.

sources.publisher: The Presidency (South Africa)
The Citizen

title: Maj-Gen Richard Shibiri dismissed; nine officers suspended
description: SAPS confirmed the dismissal of its organised crime unit head after an internal disciplinary process, and the suspension of nine officers who had served on the bid evaluation committee that awarded the Medicare24 contract.

sources.publisher: Daily Maverick

title: Final report deadline extended to 16 November 2026
description: President Ramaphosa granted an extension, moving the commission's report date from 31 August 2026 to 16 November 2026, with an evidence cut-off of 2 October 2026.

sources.publisher: The Presidency (South Africa)

title: Former IDAC head Andrea Johnson concludes her evidence
description: Johnson accepted that less intrusive means should have been used in arresting senior police officials, agreed that Gen Masemola had been wrongly grouped with fraud and corruption suspects, and said 'I have to take responsibility for all the actions that were done, intentionally or unintentionally.'

sources.publisher: IOL

title: IPID alleges extrajudicial killings by KZN task teams
description: IPID's KwaZulu-Natal deputy director Len John told the commission that a provincial task team was responsible for 149 intentional deaths and that syndicates had used police to eliminate rivals. The allegations are untested.

sources.publisher: Mail & Guardian

title: Vusimuzi 'Cat' Matlala appears under subpoena
description: Matlala declined to answer questions about the R360-million Medicare24 contract, invoking his right against self-incrimination because of pending criminal charges, and denied connections to Senzo Mchunu and Feroz Khan while acknowledging he had met Lt-Gen Mkhwanazi.

sources.publisher: Mail & Guardian

title: Parliament's ad hoc committee considers preliminary findings
description: The National Assembly's ad hoc committee's preliminary findings recorded no evidence proving a corrupt relationship between Senzo Mchunu and either Vusimuzi Matlala or Brown Mogotsi. Members remained divided on whether the 2024 disbandment of the task team was externally influenced.

sources.publisher: The Witness
